Codex review: needs real behavior proof before merge. ## What this changes This PR waits for managed Codex threads to unload before resuming their history with refreshed instructions while sibling work continues. **Example:** Conversation A fails with HTTP 400 while conversation B remains active, then A receives NEW_POLICY_BETA. - **Before:** A repeatedly refuses configuration reload because replacing the shared client would interrupt B. - **After:** A waits for its own unload notification and resumes the same thread with its history and new instructions while B continues. ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🧂 unranked krab **(1/6)** | The focused patch resolves the earlier defects and has passing exact-head CI, but this external PR has not supplied the required real-behavior evidence; persisted formats and schemas are unchanged. | | **Proof confidence** | 🧂 unranked krab **(1/6)** | Real behavior proof is necessary before merge. See [Before merge](#before-merge). | | **Patch quality** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | No actionable review findings were identified. | ## Product **Kind:** Bug fix · **Worth it:** Yes · **Fix scope:** Complete **User problem:** A failed Codex conversation cannot continue with changed instructions while another conversation keeps its shared app-server active. **Reason:** The source establishes a real remaining defect, and the area owner's cleanup adopts a focused repair while preserving external ownership and sibling protections. ## Merge readiness ⛔ **Blocked before merge - 1 item remains** This PR addresses a concrete recovery failure still present on main, and both previous findings are resolved; exact-head CI now passes. **Priority:** P1 **Reviewed head:** `76dca1a1833811b94c600216cd1176347523c256` ## Before merge - [ ] **Add real behavior proof** - The supplied evidence consists of lifecycle tests, native Gateway test results, and CI; dedicated live proof was explicitly skipped. Attach redacted terminal output or logs from a shipped Gateway showing a settled failure, changed instructions, preserved history, same-client recovery, and sibling completion, plus fresh-install and latest-stable upgrade behavior with existing settings and history intact; redact IPs, API keys, phone numbers, and non-public endpoints. After adding proof, update the PR body, then request a new review with `@clawsweeper re-review`. The PR author or someone with repository write access can request it. ## Findings None. ### Tests - Missing end-to-end proof: Supply the shipped recovery and fresh-install/latest-stable upgrade captures described below; a regression failing on the base and passing on the head has not been demonstrated.
Agent review details ### How this fits together Gateway chat sends enter the Codex plugin's thread lifecycle owner, which coordinates subscriptions, native configuration, and persisted bindings before admitting the next native turn. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Gateway chat send] --> B[Codex lifecycle owner] B --> C[Release retained subscription] C --> D[Confirm exact thread unload] D --> E[Resume original thread] E --> F[Apply current policy and start turn] B --> G[Preserve active sibling ownership] ``` ### Technical review Best possible solution: Recover through the existing per-thread lifecycle owner, preserving native history and active siblings while retaining guarded whole-client replacement as fallback. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Current-main sibling vetoes, the existing Gateway refusal scenario, and the personally inspected pinned Codex reload contract establish the failure path; no target code was executed during this review. Is this the best way to solve the issue? The revised implementation fixes the owning lifecycle boundary with an exact-thread unload receipt, bounded cancellation-aware waiting, and existing authority checks rather than interrupting the shared process. AGENTS.md: found and applied where relevant. Codex review notes: model internal, reasoning medium; reviewed against [520302d8ee63](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/520302d8ee63fd254e88042e96c393d8dc3ec461). ### Provenance checked - `Settled-failure recovery` changes intended behavior with a stated reason (6d410b5f92261e947ed8d9b99b8aeb0a5ed71a2d: Recover on a fresh client only after confirmed physical exit, with active and Incognito siblings vetoing replacement.) - `Configuration teardown observation` keeps the original intent (f5f44faeca4e68b178712152e059436f98888e50: Native resume can acknowledge ignored overrides, so exact-thread unload confirmation must precede acceptance of changed configuration.) - `Native launch override handling` changes intended behavior with a stated reason (c85129f85507b5f2e6c3bd0ce4ede29e1420195a: Preserve native override bytes and precedence through one argument-normalization owner while enforcing OpenClaw-owned launch settings.) ### Testing Proof path: in-process harness. ### Security None. ### Evidence What I checked: - **Current-main failure remains:** Fetched main retains settled-failure client replacement with active-sibling vetoes and lacks the managed per-thread unload handoff; the relevant production files match the introduction base. ([`extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle-io.ts:143`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/520302d8ee63fd254e88042e96c393d8dc3ec461/extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle-io.ts#L143), [520302d8ee63](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/520302d8ee63fd254e88042e96c393d8dc3ec461)) - **Previous findings resolved:** The introduced changes await unloading for healthy and failed managed threads, preserve bindings on unconfirmed teardown, update Gateway expectations to same-client recovery, and explicitly retain native caching in replacement controls. ([`extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle-io.ts:145`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/76dca1a1833811b94c600216cd1176347523c256/extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle-io.ts#L145), [76dca1a18338](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/76dca1a1833811b94c600216cd1176347523c256)) - **Owner-directed cleanup:** The area's established contributor steipete authored cleanup commit 6af92c4, explicitly retaining external/user-home behavior and guarded client replacement while coordinating healthy and failed teardown; it credits zhuyankarl's original fix. ([`extensions/codex/src/app-server/auth-start-options.ts:58`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/6af92c4649ea4822cf52e86dcecad525c5f39178/extensions/codex/src/app-server/auth-start-options.ts#L58), [6af92c4649ea](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/6af92c4649ea4822cf52e86dcecad525c5f39178)) - **Predecessor deliberately deferred sibling recovery:** The merged predecessor https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/149000 explicitly preserved refusal with active and Incognito siblings; obviyus's landing discussion confirms those protection controls. ([`extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle-io.ts:143`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/6d410b5f92261e947ed8d9b99b8aeb0a5ed71a2d/extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle-io.ts#L143), [6d410b5f9226](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/6d410b5f92261e947ed8d9b99b8aeb0a5ed71a2d)) - **Exact-head CI supersedes stale body status:** CI run 38684859899 attempt 3 completed successfully at the reviewed head, including the previously blocked changed-test shards and aggregate gate; current commit statuses also report success. Attach redacted terminal output or logs showing changed instructions, preserved history, and sibling completion, plus fresh-install and latest-stable upgrade behavior with settings intact; redact IPs, keys, phone numbers, and non-public endpoints. After adding proof, update the PR body, then request a new review with `@clawsweeper re-review`. The PR author or someone with repository write access can request it. - [ ] **Await teardown for healthy threads before resuming (P1)** - The new launch override sets zero unload delay for healthy idle threads too, but this condition waits only for systemError.
